meta.titre: Genetics Terminology: Genes, Alleles, Genotype and Phenotype
meta.sous_theme: Key terms of inheritance, mutation and variation

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In a family in Kumba, the grandmother has blood group O, the father has group A and his sister has group B. Neighbours ask how such differences arise. Genetics answers by using exact words: gene, allele, genotype, phenotype and others. The GCE often begins a genetics question with "define the following terms", and a precise definition earns every mark, while a vague one earns none.

items: Body cells have a nucleus, and the nucleus contains chromosomes.
Sexual reproduction begins when a male gamete fuses with a female gamete.
Children resemble their parents because they inherit characteristics from them.

sections.contenu_markdown:
A human body cell has **46 chromosomes**, arranged in **23 pairs**. A gamete (sperm or egg) has **23** chromosomes, one from each pair. At fertilisation the zygote receives 23 from each parent, which restores 46.

| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Chromosome | thread-like structure in the nucleus made of DNA and carrying genes | 23 pairs in a human cell |
| Gene | a section of DNA that controls one characteristic | gene for blood group |
| Allele | one of the alternative forms of a gene | $I^{A}$, $I^{B}$ and $i$ |
| Dominant allele | shows its effect even when only one copy is present | $T$ for tall |
| Recessive allele | shows its effect only when two copies are present | $t$ for dwarf |
| Genotype | the alleles an organism has, written as letters | $Tt$ |
| Phenotype | the characteristic that can be seen or measured | tall plant |
| Homozygous | two identical alleles | $TT$ or $tt$ |
| Heterozygous | two different alleles | $Tt$ |
| Carrier | a heterozygous person who has the recessive allele for a disorder, does not show it, but can pass it on | $Hb^{A}Hb^{S}$ |
| Codominance | both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote | group AB: $I^{A}I^{B}$ |
| Mutation | a sudden change in a gene or in the structure or number of chromosomes | sickle-cell allele |

A letter pair always uses the same letter: a capital for the dominant allele and a small letter for the recessive allele.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks about mutation
variantes.contenu_markdown: Mutations can occur by chance when DNA is copied. Their rate is raised by ionising radiation such as X-rays, by ultraviolet light and by some chemicals. Many mutations are harmful, many have no effect, and a few are useful. A mutation is passed to children only if it occurs in the cells that form gametes. Examples: a gene mutation produces the allele for sickle-cell anaemia; Down syndrome is caused by an extra chromosome.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must classify a difference between individuals
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Discontinuous variation** gives clear groups with no in-between forms, such as blood groups A, B, AB and O, or being male or female. **Continuous variation** gives a full range of values between two extremes, such as height or body mass, and is influenced by both genes and the environment.

sections.enonce_markdown: Define the terms *gene*, *homozygous* and *genotype*. Then use a person of blood group A to explain the difference between genotype and phenotype. *(8 marks)*

etapes.justification: Four tasks mean four equal parts of 2 marks each.
etapes.resultat_markdown: gene (2), homozygous (2), genotype (2), explanation of genotype and phenotype with the example (2): total 8 marks.

etapes.justification: A good definition says what a gene is and what it controls.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A gene is a section of DNA on a chromosome that controls one characteristic.

etapes.justification: Use exact words and give a letter example.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Homozygous means having two identical alleles of a gene, such as $TT$ or $tt$. Genotype is the combination of alleles that an organism has for a characteristic, such as $Tt$.

etapes.justification: The phenotype is what is observed; the genotype is the alleles behind it.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The phenotype is blood group A. The genotype may be $I^{A}I^{A}$ or $I^{A}i$, so one phenotype can come from two genotypes.

sections.conclusion_markdown: A gene is a section of DNA that controls one characteristic. Homozygous means having two identical alleles of a gene. Genotype is the set of alleles an organism has. Phenotype is the observable characteristic. A person of blood group A has this phenotype, but the genotype can be $I^{A}I^{A}$ (homozygous) or $I^{A}i$ (heterozygous).

items.erreur_markdown: "A gene and an allele are the same thing."
items.pourquoi_faux: A gene is the section of DNA that controls a characteristic. Alleles are the different forms of that gene.
items.correction_markdown: The gene for blood group has three alleles: $I^{A}$, $I^{B}$ and $i$.

items.pourquoi_faux: A dominant allele is one whose effect shows when only one copy is present. This says nothing about how common it is.
items.correction_markdown: Dominant: expressed in the heterozygote. Recessive: expressed only in the homozygote.

items.erreur_markdown: "A carrier of sickle-cell has the disease."
items.pourquoi_faux: A carrier is heterozygous. The recessive allele is present but is not expressed, so the person does not show the disorder.
items.correction_markdown: A carrier ($Hb^{A}Hb^{S}$) is healthy but can pass the allele on.

items.erreur_markdown: "Genotype is what you can see; phenotype is the letters."
items.pourquoi_faux: The two terms are reversed. Genotype is the alleles; phenotype is the visible or measurable characteristic.

items.erreur_markdown: "Every mutation causes a disease and is inherited."
items.pourquoi_faux: Many mutations have no effect. A mutation in an ordinary body cell is not passed to children.
items.correction_markdown: Only mutations in the cells that form gametes can be inherited, and not all are harmful.

items.enonce_markdown: In pea plants tall ($T$) is dominant to dwarf ($t$). For each genotype, say whether it is homozygous or heterozygous and give the phenotype: (a) $TT$, (b) $Tt$, (c) $tt$.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $TT$: **homozygous**, **tall**.

(b) $Tt$: **heterozygous**, **tall**, because the dominant allele shows.

(c) $tt$: **homozygous**, **dwarf**, because two recessive alleles are present.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) How many chromosomes are in a human body cell? (b) How many are in a sperm cell? (c) A zygote forms from a sperm and an egg. How many chromosomes does it have? (d) A baby with Down syndrome has one extra chromosome in the body cells. How many chromosomes do the cells have? (e) How many pairs does a normal body cell have?

Blood group O is caused by the recessive allele $i$, while $I^{A}$ and $I^{B}$ are codominant.

(a) Give the genotype of a person of group O.
(b) Explain how group AB shows codominance.
(c) Give the two possible genotypes of a person of group A and say which is heterozygous.
(d) Classify blood group and height as continuous or discontinuous variation.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **$ii$** (homozygous recessive).

(b) A person of genotype $I^{A}I^{B}$ makes both the A and the B characteristic, because both alleles are fully expressed, so neither hides the other.

(c) **$I^{A}I^{A}$** and **$I^{A}i$**; **$I^{A}i$** is heterozygous.

(d) Blood group is **discontinuous** variation (distinct groups); height is **continuous** variation (a whole range of values).

items_markdown: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes (23 pairs); a gamete has 23; the zygote has 46 again.
A gene controls a characteristic; alleles are its alternative forms; use a capital letter for the dominant allele and the same small letter for the recessive allele.
Genotype is the alleles; phenotype is the observable characteristic; homozygous means identical alleles, heterozygous means different alleles.
A carrier is heterozygous for a recessive disorder, is not affected, and can pass the allele on.
Codominance means both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote (group AB).
A mutation is a sudden change in a gene or chromosomes; only mutations in gamete-forming cells are inherited.
